column9: Which scientist was the first to give the atom its name, around 400 BC?
column28: Democritus named the atom around 400 BC. He did no experiments; his idea came from reasoning (philosophy). Dalton came more than 2,000 years later.
column29: Look for the scientist from ancient Greece, long before any lab experiments.

column9: The word atom comes from the Greek word *atomos*. What does *atomos* mean?
column28: *Atomos* means indivisible, which matches the early idea that the atom was the smallest piece of matter and could not be split.
column29: Democritus thought you would eventually reach a piece of matter that you could not do something to. What?

column9: Which scientist proposed the Plum Pudding Model?

column29: Which scientist used the cathode ray tube?

column9: Thomson's Plum Pudding Model included a nucleus.
column28: False. The Plum Pudding Model had no nucleus: it was a positive sphere with negative particles embedded throughout. The nucleus came with Rutherford's gold foil experiment in 1911.
column29: Was the positive charge in Thomson's model packed in the center or spread out?

column9: Dmitri Mendeleev made the first periodic table of elements in 1869. What did he organize it by?
column28: Mendeleev organized his table by atomic mass. Ordering by atomic number (number of protons) came later from Moseley in 1913. Mixing these two up is a common mistake.
column29: Mendeleev came before anyone knew about protons. What could he measure?

column9: In the Plum Pudding Model, the negative particles are embedded throughout a ___ sphere.
column28: Thomson described the atom as a positive sphere with negative particles embedded throughout, like chips in cookie dough.
column29: The whole atom is neutral, so the sphere must balance out the negative particles.

column9: Which model did John Dalton propose in 1803?
column28: Dalton's Solid Sphere Model said the atom is a solid sphere that can't get any smaller. Plum Pudding (1904), Nuclear (1911), and Electron Cloud (1926) all came later.
column29: Dalton thought the atom could not be broken into anything smaller. Which model sounds like one solid piece?

column9: Which scientists are credited with the Electron Cloud Model in 1926?
column28: Schrödinger and Heisenberg proposed the Electron Cloud Model in 1926: electrons are in shells around the nucleus, but there are no fixed orbits.
column29: This is the newest model on the timeline, so it came from the newest scientists on the list.

column9: Every atomic model so far has been wrong in some way, but each one was better than the one before it.

column29: Think about how the Plum Pudding Model improved on the Solid Sphere Model, even though it was later replaced too.

column9: Match each atomic model to its main idea.

column29: Start with the model that has the word nucleus in its name, then work forward and backward in time.

column9: In what year did Niels Bohr propose that electrons travel in fixed orbits around the nucleus?
column28: Bohr's model came in 1913, two years after Rutherford's Nuclear Model (1911). 1803 is Dalton, 1869 is Mendeleev, and 1932 is Chadwick's neutron.
column29: Bohr's model came after Rutherford's gold foil model but before the Electron Cloud Model.

column9: Which scientist proposed the Nuclear Model?
column28: Ernest Rutherford proposed the Nuclear Model in 1911 after his gold foil experiment showed a dense, positive nucleus.
column29: Which scientist fired particles at a thin sheet of metal foil?

column9: Mr. Erickson compares the Plum Pudding Model to a chocolate chip cookie. What do the chocolate chips stand for?
column28: The chips are the electrons (negative particles) and the dough is the positive sphere. There is no nucleus in this model, so nothing in the cookie stands for one.
column29: The chips are small bits spread throughout the dough. Which part of Thomson's model is spread throughout?

column9: Mendeleev's first periodic table was organized by atomic number.

column29: Protons hadn't been discovered yet in 1869. What could Mendeleev use instead?

column9: Which two scientists' contributions happened in the same year?
column28: Bohr (fixed orbits) and Moseley (atomic number) both came in 1913. Thomson was 1904 and Rutherford 1911, so those are close but not the same year.
column29: One of them changed the atom model and the other changed the periodic table.

column9: Put the atomic models in order from oldest to newest.
column28: Solid Sphere (1803), Plum Pudding (1904), Nuclear (1911), Bohr (1913), Electron Cloud (1926).
column29: The atom had to be split (negative particles) before anyone found a nucleus, and it needed a nucleus before electrons could orbit it.

column9: Put these scientists in order from earliest to latest.

column9: Match each scientist to the year of their contribution.

column29: Order the scientists first, then give the earliest date to the earliest scientist.

column17: Bohr has negative particles; the Electron Cloud Model has none

column9: Which statements describe Thomson's Plum Pudding Model? Select all that apply.

column17: The positive charge is packed in a dense nucleus
